Chunk Coordinate Normalization converts a world-space position into a canonical chunk index and local coordinate pair by adjusting the chunk index when the local coordinate falls outside the chunk's physical bounds [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly describes the normalization process: it calculates a chunk offset based on the local position, updates the chunk coordinate by adding this offset, and updates the local position by subtracting the offset multiplied by the chunk size. This effectively converts a world-space position into a canonical chunk index and local coordinate pair. The evidence also states that if the local position is outside the physical bounds (non-canonical), the normalization adjusts the chunk coordinates to ensure the final state is canonical (local position within [0, CHUNK_SIZE_METERS)).
